_help.about: The torch (design 30 Sept §AW): a burning brand carried in one hand, the first tool. Unlit until held to a flame (a lit fire, a planted torch, another torch); burns about one night; a point light with Minecraft-style falloff; can be planted in the ground. Restart after editing.
_help.burn_min: Real minutes a torch burns at full flame (the equatorial night is 48).
_help.gutter_share: The last share of its life it spends guttering: dimmer, harder flicker, the warning to head for a fire.
_help.rain_burn_scale: Burn-time multiplier in rain (storm: storm_burn_scale). douse_depth_m: water this deep puts it out.
_help.light: range_m / energy / attenuation: the falloff. gutter_energy: energy while guttering. flicker_hz / flicker_amount / wind_flicker_scale: the old flame's flicker, no longer read since the torch's head became an ember (§CP, 3 Oct): it breathes with its coal instead (see ember). sprint_flicker_scale is still read: sprinting feeds the coal air (ember.air_brighten). shadows false: no shadow map from a torch (§AG).
_help.planted: Right click the ground with a lit torch to stand it up; take it back within pickup_reach_m.
_help.lighting_reach_m: How close to a flame the torch must be held to light.
_help.bundle: Unlit torches by a camp's fire (§AW): how many, and how many game hours until the folk have made more.
_help.climb: Starting a climb with a lit torch plants it if there is ground to plant it in, otherwise it goes out (stowing puts it out; relight at a flame).
_help.resin: The resin torch's block (technique resin_torch): see resin._note.
_help.swing: (design §CN) The swing passes the flame. Left click (button: the item-in-hand action, "shoot") with the torch in hand swings it: the bare-hand swing's arc and timing (fists.gd, use_fist_arc), with the torch in the hand. At the end of the arc the flame passes between whatever it touches within reach_m (the same as lighting_reach_m), lit to unlit, either way (passes_flame): a lit torch lights a laid fire (fuel.json kindling), embers, a laid delve fire-holder (delves.json) or a planted torch (lights); an unlit torch swung through a lit fire, a lit fire-holder or a planted torch catches (takes_from). Sharing a flame costs the torch nothing (share_cost_min 0): its own burn is still the clock. It never lights the ground, standing grass, camp structures, folk or creatures (never_lights): wildfire's ignition stays a torch dropped in dry grass (§BL). A swing at a creature does nothing (creature_effect none): they answer to fire, not to the swing (§BA). Supersedes §AW's lighting ritual and the old hearths' right click (right_click_lights false): right click goes back to plain interact. log: the lines it adds to the log (§AZ). [§FA.1, 6 Oct night] In the crawler a lit torch's swing staggers a creature caught in its strike's wind-up, and never wounds it (stagger); creature_effect none stays the open world's.
_help.ember: (design §CP, recorded; built 3 Oct, Mike: "instead of the current fire animation, more of a glowing ember") The held and planted torches carry no flame: their head is the burnt end of the stick, amended the same afternoon (Mike: "not a ball"; built b7ebed5; shaders/torch_ember.gdshader); the lamps and every fire keep their flames. texels_m: texels a metre on the burnt end. crawl: how fast its cracks crawl. pulse_hz / pulse_amount: its slow breath, which the light's energy follows (Torch.ember_glow). shimmer_hz / shimmer_amount: a faint quicker shimmer on top. air_brighten: how much sprinting and wind brighten it. gutter_glow: the coal's glow while guttering: dimmer and redder, never cooler toward white or blue (§EX.6). These are the code's own defaults, written down here; the code reads this block.
_help.kinds: [NOT WIRED YET — design §CQ] Every torch is from somewhere. The folk make each camp's bundle (bundle, §AW) in tiers (kinds.bundle): first the camp's own people's light (data/peoples/*.json light: the first entry that is a kind's technique and whose genera grow where the camp stands, by the same gate as fuel.json kindling, §CA; where_no_genus names what that people uses instead, e.g. the lake folk's reed twist where no birch grows); else a torch tree that grows there (tree_kinds; the commonest within camps.json sim.loop.gather_reach_m if more than one, then tree_kinds order); else the plain brand, the torch as built. list: circle_scale scales light.range_m (the circle the dark keeps out of, dread.json torch_circle); burn_scale scales burn_min; energy_scale scales light.energy; rain_immune: rain does not shorten it (only the kinds made of fuel.json kindling's wet_ok kinds, §CN; rain_why where no genus says so); storm_burn_scale replaces the top-level one for that kind; dip: the resin_torch technique can dip it, and a dipped torch becomes resin, which keeps its numbers in the resin block (numbers_in) and adds only its circle here. technique: the techniques.json id that teaches the kind (a people's light). made: what it is, from the peoples fill. First guesses by Claude (chat), 3 Oct; the designer owns them. Check: tools/torch_kinds_check.py.
_help.ember_relight: [NOT WIRED YET — design §CQ] A carried coal brings a dead torch back. With an unlit torch in hand (relights: any with burn left, such as one that went out in water or when it was put away, or a spare from a bundle; not a burnt-out stick) and a live coal carried (the ember carrier's ember item, technique ember_carrier, one at a time as built), one press of button blows the coal into the torch: after takes_s it catches with the burn it had left, and the coal is spent (spends_coal). cancel_if: sprinting or swimming stops it. button: Claude Code's call within §CN's scheme (right click is interact): planting needs a lit torch, so this does not collide with it, and a fire in reach keeps its own interact. log: the line it adds (§AZ). Fire is never made, only carried: the coal came from a hearth (§BP).
_help.snuff: (design §ET.7; wired 6 Oct in the crawler, TorchSnuff: the open world keeps its old rules) The torch is forgiving: walking, turning and looking about never put it out (walking_and_looking). It goes out only in rare, dramatic moments, and each warns first with the coal guttering (warns_first). sprint: a flat-out sprint held for gutter_after_s seconds starts the gutter; held to out_after_s it goes out; stop sprinting during the gutter and the coal recovers over recover_s. draft: drafts blow from the builders' airways (§ET.6). An ordinary draft only leans the flame and gutters it (lean_only). A strong draft puts it out, but strong drafts are placed by the generator at marked airway mouths, never rolled at random (strong_at); each is heard and seen coming (a rising moan, dust or smoke streaming) warn_s seconds ahead, and stepping out of its line or behind cover in that time keeps the torch lit (shelter). water: deep water still douses it, at douse_depth_m as before (§AW). Out means out: relight at a lit hearth, a relit fire-holder or a carried coal (§CQ). First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct; Mike tunes by playing. [§EZ.1, 6 Oct night, Mike: "the torch should not go out, even with moving it around quickly"] moving_fast never: walking, sprinting flat out for any length of time, turning, whipping the view about and swinging it never gutter it or put it out; the sprint rule is removed in the crawler (snuff.sprint deleted with it, 7 Oct). Sprinting still feeds the coal air (ember.air_brighten). The strong airway gust and deep water are unchanged until Mike says (§EZ.4 call 1). [design §EZ.5, 6 Oct 21:47, Mike: "just water for now"] only water: in the crawler deep water (douse_depth_m) is the one thing that puts the torch out; the strong airway gust (draft) whips the flame hard (pitch_head.lean max_deg) but no longer puts it out, ordinary drafts still lean it. burns_down false: burn_min does not count down in the crawler and no torch there burns out. The open world keeps its own rules. [§FJ.4, 6 Oct 22:52, Mike: 'torches should be on a timer and can go out just like in real life'] burns_down true again: reverses §EZ.5's no burn-down in the crawler; the crawler's burn time is crawler_burn.burn_min. Moving fast still never puts it out; deep water still does; the strong gust stays as §EZ.5 left it until Mike says (§FJ.4). Built 7 Oct (Claude Code, queue 50, §EZ.1 and §EZ.5): TorchSnuff has no sprint rule; walking, sprinting for any length of time, turning, looking about and the swing never gutter the torch or put it out, and running still brightens its coal (ember.air_brighten, light.sprint_flicker_scale). The airways (crawler.json airways) never gutter it or put it out: the marked mouths keep their cycle, moan and dust (draft.warn_s is still the moan's lead), and a gust in line whips the torch hard (its smoke streams flat away from the mouth and its light flickers hard; the flame's own lean comes with pitch_head, §EZ.2); an ordinary draft leans it and flickers its light a little (crawler.json airways.flicker), no longer a gutter. So the gutter now warns only of deep water. The burn is unchanged: burn_min still counts down in the crawler (crawler_burn is §FJ.4, prompt 62). Prompt 62 (7 Oct): the crawler's torch now burns crawler_burn.burn_min (15 minutes, Mike), not the top-level burn_min.
_help.pitch_head: (design §EZ.2; wired 7 Oct in the crawler, PitchTorch: the open world keeps the burnt end) The pitch torch (Mike, 6 Oct night: "as if it's been rolled in pitch … a bit more pixelated fire rather than just the embers"). Every torch in Torchfire 1; §CQ's kinds stay with the open world. head: the stick's top wrapped and soaked in pitch, straight-sided with sides flat faces (never a ball, never rounded, §CP), length_m long and swell times the stick's radius, its wrap showing as bands steps; drips: count [min, max] runs of pitch down the stick below it, each length_m [min, max]; texels_m as ember.texels_m. colors (sRGB, painted, not lit: no shine, no specular): pitch where it is thick, thin where it is thin and bubbling just under the flame, band_edge the wrap's edges. coal: the glowing top of the wrap under the flame (ember's shader and breath, §CP). flame: the campfire's flame card (§BZ; look.json fire.flame.torch for its size and scroll), its texels texel_scale times the campfire's so it reads chunky even close in first person; sparks as the torch's flame.embers. lean: the flame leans back against your motion, per_mps degrees for each m/s, at most max_deg, stretching to sprint_stretch of its height at a sprint, and toward an airway's draft (§EV.3), settling over settle_s; it never goes out from it (§EZ.1). light: §EX.6's amber; follows the flame's flicker (§BZ noise) and the coal's breath (§CP), Claude Code's mix. smoke: as built by the flame's size, soot_scale darker toward soot (never neutral grey, R3). unlit: the pitch head alone (the bundle by the hearth). burnt_out: as built. First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct; Mike tunes by playing.
_help.stagger: (design §FA.1; wired 7 Oct in the crawler, CreatureStrike and Torch.swing_top) The torch staggers, it never wounds (Mike, 6 Oct, 22:32): a swing that lands on a creature during its wind-up (residents.json / bosses.json strike.wind_up_s) breaks its strike and it reels for reel_s; no damage. Once its strike is committed the hit goes through. lit_only, cooldown_s and noise are Claude's first guesses. The swing meets a creature at the top of its arc (half of combat.json fists.strike_s after the click), within swing.reach_m of the swing's point, in front of you (within 70° of where you look) with nothing solid between. on: the part of its strike a swing staggers it in (wind_up). noise as_sprint: a swing that lands on a creature, staggering it or not, is as loud as the crawler's sprint (noise level 1) for half a second, for anything that hears. The open world (Torchfire 2) has no creature that strikes this way, so a swing there still does nothing to one (swing.creature_effect).
_help.crawler_burn: Torches in the crawler burn on a timer (Mike): burn_min real minutes of lit time each (first guess; the open world keeps the top-level burn_min), gutter first (gutter_share, as built), then a burnt-out stick that can't be relit. You hold carry_max torches at most (Mike: 'only hold up to 3'; carry_counts_hand: the lit one in hand counts, Claude's reading). source_first: at first only the bundle by the hearth (Mike); later_sources are Claude's first guesses (the keeper remakes the bundle, bundle.remake_h_game; relit ruins' folk give some, §FF.3). Relight any torch with burn left from any flame (Mike, as built); dousing stops the clock (§FC.3). pitch_scale: the pitch technique stretches the burn (§FF.3/§FF.4, first guess). Mike, 7 Oct ("a regular torch burn time should be 15 minutes and an oil lamp gives 30 minutes"): burn_min 15 (was 20, the first guess); still to be wired by prompt 62. The clay oil lamp (30 minutes) comes back later, found in tombs (Mike, 7 Oct); not in the data yet. Wired 7 Oct (Claude Code, prompt 62; Torch.full_burn_min, carried_count, at_carry_max; CrawlerFires; CrawlerMain.take_torch): in the crawler a lit torch's burn counts down in real time from burn_min (the open world keeps the top-level burn_min) and gutters over the last gutter_share as built (dimmer, redder, §EX.6); burnt out in your hand, the charred stick drops to the floor at your feet and leaves your pack (it never catches again) and your next torch with burn left is in your hand, unlit, else your hand is empty; only lit time counts (moving fast costs nothing, §EZ.1; out or smothered it keeps its burn, douse_stops_clock; it relights from any flame, relight_any_flame, as built); carry_max: with three torches with burn left held, the one in hand counted (carry_counts_hand), the bundle gives no fourth: nothing taken, no words, a soft rustle at it; source_first: the hearth's bundle is the only source; of later_sources only bundle_remade is wired: an empty bundle is laid again torch.json bundle.remake_h_game game hours on (24: one 144-minute day) on the crawler's clock, with the log's line; restored_ruin_gift waits for §FF.3; sconces give flame only (sconces_give, as built); pitch_scale is carried, unused, until the pitch technique (§FF.3) exists.

light._help_held_scale: Design 4 Oct §EB.3 (added by Claude Code): the torch in hand's energy and range times this (about 25-30% brighter, same colour), so it pushes the dark back further; planted torches keep range_m and energy. First guess; Mike tunes it by playing.
light._help_shadows: Not read since design 6 Oct §ER.1 (Claude Code): a torch casts a soft shadow only while it is among the nearest fire lights (look.json fire_shadows, FireShadows).
light._help_color: Design 6 Oct §EX.6 (Mike: "always amber colored instead of the bluer spectrum"): every fire's light is the hearth's amber, look.json fire.light.color (#FF6E24). Was #FFB347 (§AW's first guess; §EB.3 kept it). Keep the two equal; a torch differs from a hearth in reach and strength only, never in hue.

resin._note: Design 30 Sept §BP resin torch (technique resin_torch): dipped in pine pitch it burns burn_scale times as long, energy_scale as bright, shrugs off drizzle (rain_immune) and only a storm shortens it. First guesses by Claude Code 1 Oct; the designer owns them.

log.kindling_wet: The kindling smokes and won't catch.

brand.name: Torch
brand.made: A brand of the local wood: the torch as built (§AW). Where no one's light and no torch tree fits, the folk leave these.

fatwood.name: Fatwood splints
fatwood.made: Resin-soaked heartwood split from an old pine stump (Douglas-fir pitchwood in the temperate rainforest, §CN): long and bright, and it lights wet. The taiga and old-growth folk's, and any camp's among pines.

birch_bark.name: Birch-bark torch
birch_bark.made: Strips of birch bark wedged in a split pole: a big, smoky, quick flame, and its oils keep water out (§CN). The lake folk's (their fishing torch, carried), and any camp's among birches.

candlenut.name: Candlenut string
candlenut.made: Oil-rich nuts strung on a rib, burning one after another: a small, steady light that lasts. The tropical-forest and mangrove folk's. The candlenut tree is not in the catalogue yet (§CQ), so none are made until it is added.

dammar.name: Dammar torch
dammar.made: Dipterocarp resin pounded and packed into a leaf or bark tube: a slow, bright hand light in the wet forests. The canopy folk's. Rain still shortens it: no source yet shows dammar burning damp (§CN).

fir_candle.name: Fir candle
fir_candle.rain_why: Bog pine root is fatwood: resin-soaked heartwood that lights wet (fuel.json kindling fatwood_shavings, §CN).
fir_candle.made: Thin splints of resin-black pine root dug from the peat face: hot and bright. The marsh folk's.

ichu.name: Ichu grass torch
ichu.made: A tight twist of dry tussock grass bound with grass cord: short and bright, and it dies in the wind. The highland folk's.

cane.name: Cane torch
cane.made: Dry cane, reed or bamboo bound in a bundle: bright and fast. The karst folk's, and the lake folk's reed twist where no birch grows.

rushlight.name: Rushlight
rushlight.made: A peeled rush drawn through tallow, wedged in a split stick: small, cheap and steady. The mountain folk's.

fire_stick.name: Fire stick
fire_stick.made: A twist of cured grass or a dry thorn branch carried burning at arm's length: it burns out in minutes. The savanna herders'.

resin.name: Resin torch
resin.made: The pitch dip (technique resin_torch, built, §BP): a brand or a birch-bark torch dipped at a conifer. Its burn, brightness and rain rules stay in the resin block; this adds only its circle.

log.caught: The torch caught from the coal.

flame._help_view_scale: Design 6 Oct §EZ.2 (added by Claude Code, 7 Oct): the flame on the torch in your hand, times look.json fire.flame.torch.scale. The torch in first person is drawn about half a metre from your eye, so a true-size flame (32 cm) would fill the right of the view and stream past your face when it leans back; at 0.55 it stands about a quarter of the frame tall at the bottom right (measured 119 px of 480 lines, 57 of 270). Planted torches keep the true size. Bigger is a bigger flame in hand; first guess, Mike tunes it by playing.
